description.text:
The Black Star Promos of the EX years, numbered 001 to 040 between 2003 and 2006. When Nintendo of America took over the game outside Japan from Wizards of the Coast, it began a new run of promos, with Pokémon USA creating and making the cards; Nintendo handled marketing and distribution until the end of 2005, when Pokémon USA took over.

Kyogre ex and Groudon ex opened the set through the Pokémon Ruby & Sapphire Challenge and Nintendo Power magazine. Players earned others in the e-League, which also gave jumbo winner copies, and at POP tournaments; collectors found them in EX Series tins, value packs and gift sets, Target's snack bar promotion, and the Pokémon Heroes and Jirachi: Wish Maker DVDs. The World Championships trophy cards Tropical Wind (2004), Tropical Tidal Wave (2005, 2006) and Championship Arena (2005) belong here too.

description.text: Kyogre ex and Groudon ex were the first Nintendo Black Star Promos, from the summer of 2003, when Nintendo and Pokémon USA took the English card game over from Wizards of the Coast. Holofoil copies went to some attendees of Origins Game Fair and Gen Con 2003, the last events Wizards ran, and to every player at the Ruby & Sapphire Challenge, the first Pokémon Organized Play tournaments; non-holo copies came free with Nintendo Power magazine. Hiromichi Sugiyama's Kyogre ex first appeared in Japan as promo 001/ADV-P, a gift with the February 2003 issue of CoroCoro Comic.

description.text: A jumbo copy of the Winner card, one in each League kit in October 2003, which stores gave to a winner of their choosing. Kits shipped early that month held November's jumbo Marshtomp by mistake; the Grovyle jumbo followed by mail, and organizers were told to keep the Marshtomp for the next month.

A holofoil version of Ken Sugimori's Mudkip from EX Ruby & Sapphire, with the Pokémon Organized Play logo, a Poké Ball, embossed in silver in the corner of the art. It was the first of three Hoenn starter prize cards, before Torchic and Treecko: UK tournament organizers received it in January 2004, the first promo to reach Europe before the United States. From June 2004 each sanctioned tournament in North America was sent a pack of four, one each for the top three players and the fourth for a player drawn at random.

The second of three Hoenn starter prize cards, a holofoil version of Ken Sugimori's Torchic from EX Ruby & Sapphire with the Pokémon Organized Play logo, a Poké Ball, embossed in gold. It followed Mudkip to sanctioned tournaments in the UK in early 2004, and in July 2004 to sanctioned tournaments in North America, including the side events of that month's three Stadium Challenges.

The last of three Hoenn starter prize cards, a holofoil version of Ken Sugimori's Treecko from EX Ruby & Sapphire with the Pokémon Organized Play logo, a Poké Ball, embossed in gold. Its release was held back: UK tournaments received it only in June 2004, and North American ones in August 2004. Ken Sugimori signed copies of the three cards at the 2004 World Championships, and almost every Sugimori sketch on them traces back to that event.

description.text:
Tropical Wind was the promo card of the 2004 Pokémon World Championships, held from 20 to 22 August 2004 at the Wyndham Palace Resort & Spa at Walt Disney World, near Orlando, Florida, where Japanese players won all three age groups. Each competitor received nine cards: the card in seven languages, each with a "Worlds 04" stamp, plus two insert cards. Collectors say plain unstamped copies went to spectators in far larger numbers.

The trophy versions carry a placement stamp instead: Top Sixteen, Quarter-Finalist, Semi-Finalist and, highest, Finalist. Unlike in later years, players received only the card for their best placement, so the 2004 trophy cards are scarcer than those that followed. Staff running the event got a Staff copy.

tell.text: No foil anywhere on the card.

Tropical Tidal Wave was the promo card of the 2005 Pokémon World Championships, held from 19 to 21 August 2005 at the Town and Country Resort and Convention Center in San Diego, with about 434 players. Each competitor received the card in English, Japanese, French, German, Italian, Portuguese and Spanish, plus two inserts, one advertising the coming World Championship Decks and one announcing the date and venue of the 2006 event.

The trophy versions carry a placement stamp. 2005 added a Top Thirty-Two stamp to the Top Sixteen, Quarter-Finalist, Semi-Finalist and Finalist stamps of 2004, and staff again got a Staff copy.

description.text: Championship Arena was a surprise gift for competitors at the 2005 Pokémon World Championships, held from 19 to 21 August 2005 at the Town and Country Resort and Convention Center in San Diego. It was slipped under the doors of their hotel rooms in a folded pamphlet, so unevenly that some got duplicates and others none. Spectators got no card that year, unlike 2004, when they were given an unstamped Tropical Wind 026. Two months later the same art, Ryo Ueda's arena with Mew and Celebi on its screen, became Battle Road Stadium, promo 117/PCG-P, in Japan: the prize at Battle Road Autumn 2005 (23 October to 3 November 2005), whose new six-stage tournament was also called the Battle Road Stadium, for players who beat the Pokémon Card Laboratory researcher at the sixth and last stage. Players who reached the final tournament of Battle Road Spring 2006 got it too.

A holofoil reprint of Wizards Black Star Promo 50, the Celebi given out in theaters showing Pokémon 4Ever, without the film's logo. It came in the EX Value Pack announced in November 2005, a blister of three booster packs (EX Deoxys, EX Hidden Legends and EX Sandstorm), and in an EX Collector's Carry Tin. Hajime Kusajima's art first appeared in Japan on promo 006/P, inside the official guidebook to Nintendo Space World 2001.

A holofoil reprint of Wizards Black Star Promo 53, the Suicune packed with the Pokémon 4Ever home video, without the film's logo. It came in the Deluxe Gift Sets announced in November 2005: three boxes, each with four booster packs (EX FireRed & LeafGreen, EX Team Rocket Returns, EX Unseen Forces and EX Delta Species), a deck box showing Articuno, Zapdos or Moltres, and this Suicune. It also came in an EX Collector's Carry Tin and an EX Value Pack. Atsuko Nishida's art first appeared in Japan on promo 026/P, packed with the video and DVD of Celebi: A Timeless Encounter.

All three began in Japan as Players Club promos: new members of the Pokémon Card Game Players Club in its second season, 2004, received the cosmos holofoil Moltres ex, Articuno ex and Zapdos ex, Moltres ex as 009/PLAY.

Tropical Tidal Wave returned as the promo card of the 2006 Pokémon World Championships, held from 18 to 20 August 2006 at the Hilton Anaheim in California, where 362 players competed. Its art keeps the ever-present Psyduck and adds Wailmer and Munchlax, a nod to the coming Diamond & Pearl games. As the year before, every competitor got the card in seven languages, with two insert cards.

The trophy versions carry a placement stamp, from Top Thirty-Two up to Finalist, and staff got a Staff copy.
